title.note: Game title, glossary keep; the guide keeps game titles in English because players search the English title.

hud.cast.note: Verbal-noun button, as the guide asks for one-word buttons; "bedobás" is the anglers' word for casting the line in. 7/8.

hud.reel.note: Verbal noun of "behúz" (pull the line and fish in); same word inside the pass name Autobehúzás. Anglers also say "orsózás", less clear to kids. 7/8.

hud.bait_left.note: Label form, so 0, 1 and 12 all read right; "csali" is the everyday angler word for bait.

catch.success.note: Restructured: no suffix can attach to {fish}, so the accusative sits on the generic "halat" and the inserted words follow a colon in the nominative: "Kifogtál egy halat: Ritka Aranyponty!". The tier label's capital mid-sentence is the guide's accepted item-name style.

catch.escaped.note: "It" made explicit as the generic "a hal"; "elszökött" = got away. Trailing ellipsis kept.

catch.new_record.note: For the developer: {weight} arrives as "12.4"; Hungarian writes a decimal comma, "12,4 kg", and may read "12.4" as a date. Format the number per locale in code.

fish.golden_carp.note: One-word compound like "aranyhal" (goldfish); ponty = carp. Nominative base form, so it also works inserted into catch.success.

fish.lantern_eel.note: lámpás (lantern) + angolna (eel) as one word, after the real Hungarian "lámpáshal" (lanternfish); keeps the glowing-lantern idea. 13/18.

rarity.mythic.note: Tier ladder Ritka < Legendás < Mitikus, the usual game tier words; adjective form that also reads right before a fish name in catch.success.

shop.rods.note: Short form of the term "Horgászbotok" (12), which is over the 10 budget. Anglers call rods "bot" every day and the tab sits in a fishing shop; but gamers also say "botok" for bots, so use "Horgászbotok" if the tab fits 12.
shop.rods.blind_remark: bare 'bot' also just means 'stick'; reads as fishing rods only from the shop context

shop.equip.note: Verbal-noun button with the same root as the label "Felszerelve". 11 is one over the estimated 10; if it clips, "Használat" (9, "Use") is the fallback.
shop.equip.review_reason: A bare "Felszerelés" reads first as the noun gear/equipment (the blind back-translation gave "Equipment"), all the more in a fishing game where "horgászfelszerelés" is the gear, and it is 11 against the estimated 10; "Használat" (9) is the verbal-noun Use button Minecraft Bedrock players know and still pairs clearly with the label "Felszerelve".

shop.equipped.note: State form (adverbial participle) of the button's verb, so button and label differ as the context asks; Hungarian has no agreement to worry about. 11/11.

shop.free.note: Price-label adjective "free of charge". 8/8; "Ingyen" (6) also works.

shop.buy_robux.note: Guide's reference pattern: te-imperative because the button carries a price; Robux kept with -ért attached directly, no suffix on {price}. 18/20.

pass.auto_reel.note: Same verb as hud.reel (Behúzás) with the joined prefix auto-, as in Microsoft's "Automentés"; "Automatikus behúzás" (19) is over 14. The pass name in Creator Hub should match.
pass.auto_reel.blind_remark: coined compound; understandable but not a standard word

pass.lucky_bait.text: A Szerencsecsalival dupla eséllyel fogsz ritka halat!
pass.lucky_bait.note: Pass name built like the guide's "Szerencsebájital" (szerencse = luck, csali = Bait). Restructured to "With Lucky Bait you catch rare fish at double the chance"; the -val suffix sits inside the bold tag, fine for a fixed item name. "ritka" is the same word as the tier Ritka.

sell.all.note: Te-imperative because the button carries an object (guide); the verbal-noun form "Összes eladása" (14) is longer. 13 is one over the estimated 12 and nothing shorter keeps "all".

sell.done.note: Nouns after numbers stay singular in Hungarian, so 1 and 12 both read right; suffixes sit on the nouns ("halat", "érméért"), never on the params.

sell.prompt.note: Key plus verbal noun, the guide's prompt pattern; a sentence like "Nyomd meg az E-t" breaks if the key changes. For the developer: phones and consoles have no E key; ProximityPrompt ActionText "Eladás" with the built-in key hint would serve everyone.

ascend.button.note: "Felemelkedés" = rise in the figurative sense, the natural word for Ascend; not religious (the Ascension is "mennybemenetel") and not climbing. 12 is over the estimated 10; if the button cannot grow, "Rangemelés" (10, rank-up) is the fallback, and ascend.confirm must change with it.
ascend.button.review_reason: A single unbreakable 12-character word against an estimated 10 on a button whose screen and size are unknown, so it may clip; check it in Studio with hu-hu, and if the button cannot grow or scale, switch the term to "Rangemelés" (10) in ascend.button, ascend.confirm and terms.json together.

ascend.confirm.text: Jöhet a felemelkedés? Elölről kezded, de {bonus}%-kal gyakrabban fogsz ritka halat.
ascend.confirm.note: "Jöhet a felemelkedés?" (ready to ascend?) mirrors the guide's rebirth line; "now" dropped as filler. "%-kal" is right for any number because the suffix follows the spoken "százalék". Medium only because it carries the Ascend term choice.

weather.storm.text: Jön a vihar! Ritka halak kapnak a csalira!
weather.storm.note: "Kap a csalira" is the anglers' verb for biting; "harap" would be a calque. "a csalira" added so kids don't read "kapnak" as "they receive".

quest.catch_n.note: Moonlit Bay -> "Holdfényes-öböl", spelled like Hungarian bay names ("Finn-öböl"); locative "-öbölben". "{n} halat": the noun stays singular after any number, so n = 1 reads right.

friends.boost.text: Ha a barátaiddal horgászol, +{percent}% szerencsét kapsz
friends.boost.note: Statement as a "ha" (if/when) clause, not an order; no space before %, and the suffix sits on "szerencsét", not on the param.

trade.sent.note: No suffix can attach to {player}, so the dative sits on the fixed noun "játékosnak" (the guide's trick). 31/33.

trade.accept.note: {player} is the subject, so no suffix and no gender; "cserekérésedet" = your trade request, same word as trade.sent.

codes.enter.note: Guide's reference placeholder; the definite "a kódot" is how Hungarian placeholders read. 14/20.

afk.kicked.text: Túl sokáig voltál inaktív, ezért leállt a horgászás.
afk.kicked.note: Says only that fishing stopped, as the source does; no removal from the server added. "inaktív" is the common gaming word for idle.

settings.sfx.note: Usual game-settings term; "Hanghatások" (11) is also used. 14/18.

event.ends.note: Guide's reference; postposition "múlva", no suffix on {time}. For the developer: {time} arrives as "2d 4h", letters that mean nothing in Hungarian; send "2 nap 4 ó" (CLDR short forms nap, ó, p, mp).

daily.streak.text: Sorozat: {day}. nap! Gyere vissza holnap még több jutalomért!
daily.streak.note: Label form "Streak: day {day}" with an ordinal period, so day 1 reads right and no article sits before the number. "for more" made explicit as "more rewards".

tip.night.text: Tipp: néhány hal csak éjjel kap a csalira.
tip.night.note: "Tipp:" is the Hungarian spelling, lowercase after the colon; "kap a csalira" (bite) as in weather.storm.

group.join.text: Lépj be a csoportunkba 50 ingyenes csaliért!
group.join.note: "a csoportunkba" (our group), as the guide writes it; 50 kept, and the noun stays singular after the number.

leaderboard.biggest.note: The anglers' idiom; the board lists weights, so it reads as heaviest. "Legnehezebb fogás" (17) could also read as "hardest catch".
